subject: using mlg.filter to produce a genclone object for mll

messages.author: c59ab11b418f0190
messages.subject: using mlg.filter to produce a genclone object for mll
parts:
Hi there, apologies if this has already been covered somewhere but I can't find much information on using the mlg.filter function. I have a dataset of 9k SNPs, no missing data but I suspect there might be clones in there. 

I have two queries:

1. I don't quite understand how to determine the threshold to apply (I read about the cutoff_predictor function but have had little luck in actually using it)

2. When I've played around with arbitrary thresholds, I get a list assigning all samples to a given mll but how do I then convert this information to a genclone object to then do clone corrected analysis with?

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] using mlg.filter to produce a genclone object for mll
parts: 1. I don't quite understand how to determine the threshold to apply (I read about the cutoff_predictor function but have had little luck in actually using it)

The choice of threshold is still a bit wobbly, I'm afraid. In short, you'll want to use the functions filter_stats() and cutoff_predictor(): https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/reference/cutoff_predictor.html#examples 

The best method is to look for an initial, small peak in the histogram of pairwise genetic distances and set the threshold to be between that peak and the larger peak (https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.12550). The filter_stats() function will show you this histogram with an overlay of the number of multilocus lineages (MLL) present after a given threshold. The number of thresholds will always be the number of MLGs minus one. You can see that here: https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/articles/mlg.html#tie-breakers-algorithms where there is a small peak that ends at a distance of ~0.11 that would collapse 71 MLG to 48 MLL. 

The cutoff_predictor() function will take the threshold output of filter_stats() and try to find the largest gap between thresholds.

2. When I've played around with arbitrary thresholds, I get a list assigning all samples to a given mll but how do I then convert this information to a genclone object to then do clone corrected analysis with?

If you have your threshold chosen, you can apply to your genclone/snpclone object like so (assuming myData is the name of your object):

mlg.filter(myData) <- myThreshold + .Machine$double.eps^0.5

This is detailed in https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/articles/mlg.html#filtered-contracted 

So, if we were to follow the example of https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/reference/cutoff_predictor.html#examples, we would use the results of cutoff_predictor() to set the threshold:


data(Pinf)
pinfreps <- fix_replen(Pinf, c(2, 2, 6, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 2))
pthresh  <- filter_stats(Pinf, distance = bruvo.dist, replen = pinfreps,
                         plot = TRUE, stats = "THRESHOLD", threads = 1L)

# prediction for farthest neighbor
cutoff_predictor(pthresh$farthest)
# [1] 0.1132221

mlg.filter(Pinf, dist = bruvo.dist, replen = pinfreps) <- cutoff_predictor(pthresh$farthest)
Pinf
# 
# This is a genclone object
# -------------------------
# Genotype information:
# 
#    48 contracted multilocus genotypes
#       (0.11) [t], (bruvo.dist) [d], (farthest) [a]
#    86 tetraploid individuals
#    11 codominant loci
# 
# Population information:
# 
#     2 strata - Continent, Country
#     2 populations defined - South America, North America

Hope that helps!
Zhian
